newsitem.title: USA: Angry Texas mother killed kids, prosecutors charge.
newsitem.headline: Angry Texas mother killed kids, prosecutors charge.

text.p: A Texas woman killed her two young sons because she was angry at losing her good looks and financial freedom, prosecutors said Monday at the opening of the murder trial of Darlie Routier.
They described Routier as "a self-centred woman, a materialistic woman" plagued by weight problems and the demands of a floundering family business.
The defence scoffed at the charges and said the police got the wrong person.
Routier, 27, is accused of stabbing to death sons Devon, 6, and Damon, 5, as they slept in the living room of their comfortable home in Rowlett, Texas, near Dallas on June 6.

Prosecutor Greg Davis told the jury of seven women and five men that Routier was depressed because she had been unable to lose weight gained during her pregnancy with a third son, Drake, now 14 months old, and was taking diet pills at the time of the murders.
"She was no longer the glamorous, blond centre of attention," he said.
Also, the electronics business she and husband Darin Routier ran was struggling so that by June 6, their bank accounts were virtually empty, Davis said.
"She was becoming very angry that she could not have the lifestyle she was accustomed to -- the vacations, the buying sprees and the freedom," he said.
But defence attorney Richard Mosty argued that prosecutors had the wrong person because police bungled the investigation.
"They developed tunnel vision, or maybe it was more like a rifle scope. They focused their crosshairs on Darlie and never took them off," he said.
Mosty described Routier as a "devoted mother" who loved her children. "In the blink of an eye, she changes from a doting mother to a psychotic killer? It's not possible," he said.

Routier said the murderer was a male intruder, dressed in dark clothes and a baseball cap, who broke into her home early on June 6 and killed the two boys "like an animal killing sheep" before stabbing her and escaping.
But prosecutors accused her of inventing the story about an intruder and of stabbing herself in the neck and shoulder to back up her story.
Police arrested Routier 12 days after the murders, saying her oral statement was full of inconsistencies. She faces the death penalty if convicted.
Her husband Darin, who was upstairs sleeping with the couple's infant son at the time of the murders, was not charged by police and insisted his wife is innocent.

State District Judge Mark Tolle moved the trial from Dallas to Kerrville, 80 miles northwest of San Antonio, Texas, because of intense publicity. He also put a gag order on those involved in the case.
